To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the thermal conductivity of a particulate food is dependent on the particle size, shape and orientation, and on the porosity; and (ii) the thermal conductivity can be estimated using the geometric model.

the thermal conductivity bounds analysis is a useful tool for the evaluation of thermal conductivity data and that the geometric model provides the most accurate first approximation thermal conductivity predictions of particulate foods.

(1) the thermal conductivity of a particulate food can be predicted using the geometric model; (2) the geometric model is the most accurate model considered; (3) the thermal conductivity data for most particulate foods are consistent with the geometric model and the bounds analysis; and (4) the thermal conductivity values for some particulate foods, such as cocoa powder, are not consistent with the geometric or the bounds models.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the thermal conductivity data for the five foods considered in this study were in the range 0.03–0.30 Wm–1 K– 1, and that the thermal conductivity prediction models considered were accurate enough for most engineering applications.

the geometric model is recommended for use to predict the thermal conductivity of foods with particle size less than 1 mm, and the effective medium model for foods with particle size greater than 1 mm.

the thermal conductivity data for the particulate foods measured in this study are in agreement with those published in the literature, and that the thermal conductivity range of 0.03 to 0.30 is valid for particulate foods provided the porosity is >25% and the particle diameter is >0.1 μm.

, provided the porosity is known or can be estimated with reasonable accuracy, the thermal conductivity of most particulate foods can be predicted with reasonable accuracy by the geometric model.
the thermal conductivity data for most particulate foods is reliable and the geometric model provides a reasonable first approximation prediction for the thermal conductivity of these foods.

the thermal conductivity for particulate foods is highly sensitive to the porosity of the material, and that the thermal conductivity is likely to fall within the range of 0.03 and 0.3 W m–1K–1, provided the porosity is above 25%.
